title: Puffed-up Inner Rings and Razor-thin Outer Rings in Structured Protoplanetary Disks
question: How does the vertical dust scale height differ between inner and outer rings of resolved double-ring protoplanetary disks, measured from azimuthal intensity variations in ALMA Band 6 continuum rings?

data.angular_resolution: Beams: V1094 Sco 0.074'' x 0.096''; AA Tau 0.061'' x 0.068''; LkCa 15 tapered to circular 0.05'' x 0.05''
data.sensitivity: rms measured in emission-free annuli; LkCa 15 9.3 mJy/beam (0.09 K) without JvM correction (other disks given in Table in K only)

recipe.method: Use published Band 6 images for AS 209, HD 163296, GM Aur, LkCa 15; for V1094 Sco and AA Tau, pipeline-calibrate archival data, self-calibrate in CASA 6.4.1 (short baselines first, then combined) and image with Briggs weighting 1 and 2, without primary-beam or JvM correction
assumptions: Missing primary-beam correction is negligible because disk emission is much smaller than the primary beam

recipe.method: Compute rms in concentric annuli, adopt the median beyond the emission where the radial rms profile is flat

recipe.goal: Set disk geometry, extract radial profiles and define ring masks
recipe.method: Find the image center by rotating the image by 180 degrees and minimising the squared residuals of the difference; adopt PA and inclination from literature; extract radial intensity profile with gofish; fit only where the azimuthally averaged intensity exceeds half the ring peak
key_parameters: Ring selection: radially resolved, fitted Gaussian width greater than the beam size, and sufficiently sharp; exactly two rings per disk
assumptions: PA and inclination taken from previous studies

recipe.goal: Fit the ring model to the image with MCMC
recipe.method: Fit each ring with an empirical model: Gaussian vertical optical depth profile, two half-Gaussian radial widths, single ring temperature, I_los = (1-exp(-tau_los)) B_nu(T_ring), convolved with the beam; five free parameters per ring (T, r0, w_i, w_o, H_d)
key_parameters: 32 walkers, run until the autocorrelation time converges
Burn-in of twice the maximum autocorrelation time

recipe.goal: Summarise posteriors and set upper limits on scale height
recipe.method: Report the 50th percentile with 16th and 84th percentiles as 1 sigma; where the MLE of H_d is below the 16th percentile and near zero, quote the 84th percentile as an upper bound

recipe.goal: Derive gas scale height and dust settling coefficient alpha_z/St
recipe.method: H_g = c_s/Omega_K with isothermal hydrostatic gas; three temperatures (fitted ring T, flaring-disk T with phi = 0.02, CO-isotopologue mid-plane T); alpha_z/St = (H_d/H_g)^2 for partially settled dust
key_parameters: flaring angle phi = 0.02 for the flaring-disk temperature
assumptions: Dust vertical diffusion and settling in equilibrium
Gas temperature uncertain; H_g in the main table uses the fitted ring temperature equal to the gas temperature

recipe.goal: Test whether grain-size (Stokes number) differences can explain the inner/outer contrast
recipe.method: Assume fragmentation-limited St with constant v_frag and delta_frag = alpha_z, giving alpha_z,1/alpha_z,2 = sqrt(C T2/T1) with C = (alpha_z,1/alpha_z,2)(St2/St1); compare lower limit on C with the observed temperature ratio
assumptions: Constant fragmentation velocity between rings; vertical diffusion dominates the collision velocity so delta_frag = alpha_z

score_reason: Data are public and the model, likelihood and sampler are specified, with numeric tables, but self-calibration/imaging details for two disks, parameter references and MCMC settings are missing and no code is released.
rediscovery_reason: Public images exist for four of the six disks, the model equations and likelihood are given, and the main results are numeric (scale heights, alpha_z/St), so the fit can be redone for those disks, though two disks need unstated reprocessing.
